unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 9 (AFTER PREP)-LEVEL: B2.1 - THEME 6: LIFE IN THE WORLD & CULTURE

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will explore the theme ''Life in the World and Culture'' by focusing on global cuisines, food habits, and cultures, cultural diversity through international sports, films, and musical events, and the impact of globalisation on everyday life. Students will design ''a cultural portfolio'' in which they choose one country to research and present its unique food traditions, popular cultural events, and important contributions to global sports or arts. They will also examine how globalisation has influenced these traditions, such as the fusion of cuisines or the international popularity of certain sports and films. The portfolio will include visuals, descriptions, and personal reflections on what they have learnt about the interconnectedness of cultures worldwide. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''life in the world and culture with its components such as global cuisines, food habits and cultures; cultural diversity and international sports, films and musical events; impact of globalisation on everyday life'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student after prep year 9 of an upper secondary school may know what global cuisines, food habits and cultures; cultural diversity and international sports, films and musical events; impact of globalisation on everyday life mean in their as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in the after prep year 9 of an upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''life in the world and culture'' and also some necessary structures in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students after prep year 9 of an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''life in the world and culture with its components such as global cuisines, food habits and cultures; cultural diversity and international sports, films and musical events; impact of globalisation on everyday life'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss about the poster and/ or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To talk about global cuisines, food habits, and cultures in English by using target vocabulary. Activity 1: Students write a short paragraph about global cuisines or cultural diversity using at least five target vocabulary and grammatical items (e.g. modals for probability, necessity, or advice). For example, they might describe a dish such as Turkish Dolma (stuffed peppers) by explaining its ingredients, preparation, and cultural significance. After writing, they create a slide with visuals (e.g. a picture of the dish). Then they present their slide and paragraph to the class, explaining globalisation or cultural habits. The teacher provides feedback on the use of language including target vocabulary, grammar, and also their presentation skills. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To talk about global cuisines and their impact on people in English by using target vocabulary. Activity 1: Understanding Global Cuisines and Their Influence The teacher prepares a short paragraph about global cuisines and their influence on people. Students read the paragraph and answer simple comprehension questions to practice target vocabulary and target grammar. Reading Text (Simplified): ''Global cuisines are very popular today. People can try many different flavours such as spicy or sweet dishes from all over the world. For example, sushi is a famous Japanese dish made with rice and fish. To make it, chefs chop fresh ingredients and combine them carefully. Eating healthy food like sushi can be good for your nutrition. You should also avoid eating too much sugar because it may cause health problems like obesity. If you want to cook healthy meals, you need to use fresh and balanced ingredients''. Questions: True or False: Sushi is made with rice and fish. What is a good example of healthy food from Japan? Which word means ''too much weight'' because of unhealthy food? Complete the sentence: ''To make sushi, chefs ______ fresh ingredients''. Students read their answers aloud to the class. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback on the use of language including accuracy and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
